PAPERS.title: Validation of PurpleAir PM2.5 Sensors in Temperate Urban Environments
PAPERS.pm: PurpleAir PA-II PM2.5 (cf_1 vs atm outputs) co-located with reference; RH from PA and weather station
PAPERS.n: Co-location in Philadelphia across summer and spring plus a one-year re-evaluation. Best performance came from the nationwide Barkjohn (2021) correction applied to the mean of the two channels' atm outputs: RMSE 1.64 ug/m3, MBE 0.10 ug/m3, R2 0.683 at 1 h and 24 h, ahead of locally derived corrections. RH source (on-board vs weather station) changed R2 by only 0.04. After a year in the field R2 fell to 0.567. Limitation: R2 0.68 at low temperate concentrations means RMSE is the honest metric and the R2 drop partly reflects a narrower concentration range in the later period, not drift alone - the abstract does not separate them. Applying Barkjohn, derived on cf_1, to atm outputs is off-label. Relevance: high - direct evidence that a national correction can beat local fitting, and that year-one degradation needs scheduled re-co-location.

PAPERS.short: SEER wildfire PM2.5 head and neck cancer 2026
PAPERS.title: Wildfire Air Pollution Exposure and Head and Neck Cancer Incidence
PAPERS.pm: County-level wildfire-specific PM2.5 (exceedance days, any exposure, % days > 5 ug/m3), 0-10-y lags
PAPERS.endpoint: Head and neck cancer incidence by subsite
PAPERS.n: SEER 2016-2022, county-level DLNM with 0-10-year lags, adjusted for tobacco, alcohol and demographics with county random effects. Cumulative RR per additional smoke-exceedance day 1.06 (1.04-1.09); any annual exposure 1.41 (1.24-1.60); per percentage-point of days >5 ug/m3 1.23 (1.13-1.33). Larynx largest (1.13, 1.07-1.19 per day), oropharynx 1.09. Limitation: ecological county-level exposure and covariates, a ten-year lag fitted on seven years of incidence, and wildfire-exposed western counties differ in screening and HPV epidemiology; the p16 stratification is the right control but its result is truncated in the abstract. Relevance: moderate-high - a second smoke-cancer signal this week (cf. 13 Oct China), both favouring upper aerodigestive sites.

PAPERS.title: Rising global population coexposure to heatwaves and landscape fire-sourced air pollution
PAPERS.pm: Landscape fire-sourced PM2.5 (modelled) coincident with heatwave days
PAPERS.n: Global 2000-2019: 55.9% of the population lived where heatwave-smoke coexposure increased; 916 million people/year had at least one coexposure day, rising by 287 million per decade; mean coexposure days per person rose from 1.0 to 1.7. Of the 5.5 billion person-day/decade increase, 70.5% was intensity and 29.5% population growth; low-HDI countries carried the most. Limitation: the fire-PM product is model-derived with no stated threshold sensitivity, and 'coexposure day' is a binary that discards concentration. Relevance: moderate - joint heat-smoke days are also when optical sensors are most biased (low RH, fresh smoke), so the exposure most in need of measurement is the hardest to measure cheaply.

PAPERS.title: Air pollution is associated with sex-specific longitudinal changes in astrocytic and neuroinflammatory processes linked to cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease at-risk individuals
PAPERS.pm: LUR NO2, PM10, PM2.5, PM2.5 absorbance
PAPERS.endpoint: 3-year change in CSF GFAP, IL-6 and AD biomarkers; executive function
PAPERS.n: 226 cognitively unimpaired middle-aged adults at elevated AD risk with baseline and 3-year CSF. Higher traffic-related exposure associated with longitudinal increases in GFAP and IL-6, mainly in women; GFAP partially mediated associations with worsening executive and attentional performance. Limitation: no effect sizes in the abstract; n=226 split by sex across four correlated pollutants and many biomarkers is a multiplicity problem, and single-address LUR estimates ignore time-activity. Relevance: moderate - CSF longitudinal biology is rare, but this is hypothesis-generating at this n.

PAPERS.title: Ambient Air Pollution Health Impacts in High-Income Countries, Part II: A Case Study in the United Arab Emirates
PAPERS.pm: Anthropogenic PM and ozone, 2019-2022 vs 2008
PAPERS.n: Attributable deaths from anthropogenic PM and ozone in Abu Dhabi rose from 231 (90% UI 59-427) in 2008 to 1,249 (507-2,169) in 2019-2022, despite air quality holding roughly steady while population doubled. The increase reflects population growth, better health records and, mainly, steeper concentration-response functions. Limitation: a fivefold change driven largely by swapping CRFs is a change in assumptions, not in burden; the 'anthropogenic' split in a dust-dominated desert regime is itself model-dependent. Relevance: moderate - shows how far CRF choice swamps measured trends, which bounds what better monitoring alone can change.

PAPERS.title: Neighborhood-Scale O3, NO2, and PM2.5 in Washington, D.C. from a 1 x 1 km2 WRF-SMOKE-CMAQ Framework
PAPERS.pm: Hourly O3, NO2, PM2.5 at 1 km (2017)
PAPERS.n: 1 km CMAQ for 2017: hourly O3 r up to 0.7; NO2 biased -14 to -29% from unresolved near-road gradients. NO2's coefficient of variation exceeded O3's and was more than three times PM2.5's; urban-core O3 was 4-11% lower from titration. Moving from 4 to 1 km changed population-weighted exposure by only -1.5 to -3% for PM2.5. Limitation: evaluation against a handful of AQS sites in one city cannot test intra-urban gradients - the very thing 1 km is meant to add. Relevance: high - quantifies that PM2.5 is the spatially smoothest pollutant, so dense PM2.5 networks buy less spatial information than NO2 networks would.

PAPERS.title: Elevated Outdoor O3 Can Sustain New Particle Formation and Growth Indoors
PAPERS.pm: Indoor particle number size distributions; ventilated O3; limonene addition
PAPERS.geo: Not stated (aged unoccupied office, high-O3 region)
PAPERS.n: In an authentic office in a high-O3 region, mechanical ventilation supplied enough O3 that indoor new particle formation was VOC-limited, not O3-limited; limonene addition drove growth at 20-100 nm/h, one to two orders above outdoor rates, with meaningful mass from grown particles. Limitation: one building, injected limonene rather than real product use, and no occupancy. Relevance: high - indoor UFP and secondary mass from cleaning products are invisible to PM2.5-only indoor sensors until particles grow past ~300 nm.

PAPERS.title: Association between household fuel use and childhood undernutrition in Pakistan: evidence from a National survey
PAPERS.pm: Household air pollution proxied by self-reported primary cooking fuel
PAPERS.endpoint: Composite anthropometric failure, stunting, wasting, underweight
PAPERS.n: 4,224 under-fives; 45.4% with anthropometric failure, 37.7% stunted. Polluting vs clean fuels: CIAF OR 1.16 (1.04-1.31), stunting 1.16 (1.03-1.31), wasting 1.13 (1.00-1.29), underweight 1.17 (1.04-1.32); dung strongest. Limitation: fuel type is a wealth marker as much as an exposure, and with no measured PM the residual socioeconomic confounding is plausibly the size of the effect; cross-sectional. Relevance: moderate - the standard HAP proxy, and a reminder of why personal-monitor substudies inside DHS-type surveys are needed.

PAPERS.title: Impact of Holika Dahan on ambient PM2.5 and associated health risks in an urban environment of Lucknow, India
PAPERS.pm: Night-time PM2.5 mass and chemistry (tracers, ATR-FTIR), HYSPLIT, AERMOD
PAPERS.n: Pre-, during- and post-Holika Dahan nights at a residential and a commercial site: PM2.5 rose 2.0x and 1.4x; burning tracers 1.2-2.7x; PCA/HCA identified festival biomass burning as the dominant source; AERMOD placed hotspots out to 1.2-1.5 km. Hazard indices stayed below USEPA limits. Limitation: two sites over three nights, and a chronic-dose hazard index applied to a single-night event is the wrong risk metric. Relevance: moderate - a short, intense, spatially bounded event of exactly the kind a dense network resolves and two filter sites do not.

PAPERS.title: Time series evidence on air quality transitions under urban shock during COVID-19 shutdown in Delhi-NCR, India
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5, PM10, NOx, SO2, CO, O3 at 10 CAAQMS stations
PAPERS.n: Ten regulatory stations across pre-, during- and post-COVID periods analysed with ARIMA, PCA, change-point detection and recurrence quantification: significant reductions and altered temporal dynamics during lockdown, with meteorology and secondary formation relatively more important. Limitation: no deweathering is described, so lockdown effects are confounded with seasonal meteorology; the lockdown literature on Delhi is saturated. Relevance: low.

PAPERS.title: PAH-associated health risk from ultrafine particles: an urban field study
PAPERS.pm: UFP respiratory deposition (MALDA) and size-segregated UFP-bound PAHs
PAPERS.n: Three Houston sites: UFP respiratory deposition measured directly with the Mobile Aerosol Lung Deposition Apparatus, combined with size-segregated PAH analysis to estimate deposited PAH mass. Both carcinogenic and non-carcinogenic risks were within acceptable levels. Limitation: no numbers in the abstract; PAH risk is one narrow axis of UFP toxicity, so 'acceptable' does not translate to UFP being benign. Relevance: moderate - measured deposited dose rather than ambient concentration is the right exposure metric and is rarely available.

PAPERS.title: Optical properties and shape-dependent retrievals of the imaginary part of the refractive index of freshly emitted Saharan dust
PAPERS.pm: Size-resolved SSA, AAE, asymmetry, MAE/MSE; retrieved imaginary refractive index
PAPERS.n: In-situ optics during active emission events (Sept 2019): SSA for PM2.5 (PM10) 0.95 (0.94) at 370 nm and 0.97 (0.96) at 660 nm; AAE to 2.5 (2.0) from iron oxides; MAE fell from 0.30 to 0.15 m2/g at 370 nm with size. The imaginary index was retrieved under prescribed shape and density. Limitation: the retrieval depends on the shape assumption it is titled after, and a single campaign. Relevance: moderate - mass scattering efficiency shifting with size is the physics behind optical sensors' coarse-dust under-response; these values are usable priors for a dust correction.

PAPERS.title: Seasonal ambient temperature and particulate matter as discriminators of hyperemesis gravidarum severity: a retrospective comparative observational study
PAPERS.pm: Ambient PM10, SO2 and temperature (regional)
PAPERS.n: 211 HG patients: temperature (AUC 0.799) and PM10 (AUC 0.754) discriminated severe from non-severe ketonuria; SO2 did not. The PM10 association attenuated after adjustment for temperature. Limitation: hospital series with no control group, ecological exposure, and PM10 and temperature are seasonally collinear - the attenuation says PM10 was largely a season marker. Relevance: low.

PAPERS.title: Vitamin C attenuates PM2.5-induced thyroid dysfunction and mitophagy dysregulation by rebalancing ER-mitochondrial Ca2+ dynamics
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 instillation (rats) and FRTL5 thyrocyte exposure
PAPERS.endpoint: Thyroid function, ER stress, mitochondrial Ca2+, mitophagy
PAPERS.n: Female rats and FRTL5 thyrocytes: PM2.5 impaired thyroid function and histology, triggered ER stress, remodelled MAM proteins (IP3R1, GRP75, VDAC1), caused mitochondrial Ca2+ overload, ROS, depolarisation, PINK1/Parkin changes, GPX4 loss and Fe2+ accumulation; 4-PBA, 2-APB, Mdivi-1 and vitamin C each mitigated damage. Limitation: doses not given in the abstract and likely supra-environmental. Relevance: low - mechanism for a thyroid signal that the epidemiology (13 Oct fire-PM thyroid cancer) has not yet tied to function.

PAPERS.title: PM2.5 promotes migration of hepatocellular carcinoma by targeting miR-25
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 exposure of MHCC97H cells and mouse tumour models
PAPERS.n: PM2.5 lowered E-cadherin, raised vimentin and miR-25 and increased MHCC97H migration; miR-25 mimics amplified and inhibitors attenuated the effect; mouse models showed enhanced tumour growth and invasion. Limitation: single cell line, unstated doses, and a single-miRNA mechanism for a pleiotropic exposure. Relevance: low.

PAPERS.title: Effects of synbiotic versus omega-3 supplementation on total antioxidant capacity in adolescents exposed to ambient air pollution: A randomized double-blind controlled trial
PAPERS.pm: Ambient air pollution (not measured at individual level)
PAPERS.n: 70 healthy adolescents aged 10-18, 8 weeks synbiotic (n=38) vs omega-3 (n=32). TAC rose within both arms (839.8 to 903.4 and 898.6 to 953.3 umol/L) with no between-group difference (p=0.75). Limitation: active-comparator trial with no placebo arm, so within-arm rises cannot be separated from regression to the mean or seasonal change; exposure is not measured, so 'exposed to air pollution' is residence in Isfahan. Relevance: low.

PAPERS.title: Differential effects of PM2.5 constituents on tuberculosis infection and disease progression in 40,379 student close contacts
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 constituents
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates a constituent-resolved analysis of PM2.5 and latent infection and progression among 40,379 student close contacts of TB cases. Recorded for coverage; no estimate inferred. Relevance: moderate - a large contact cohort is an unusually clean design for an infection endpoint.

PAPERS.title: Association between occupational LiFePO4 exposure and cardiac autonomic function: a cross-sectional study of cathode material production workers
PAPERS.pm: Occupational LiFePO4 particle exposure
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates a cross-sectional study of battery-cathode workers' LiFePO4 particle exposure and cardiac autonomic function. Recorded for coverage. Relevance: moderate - battery-material dust is an emerging occupational particle class with little exposure data.

PAPERS.title: Air purifier performance in an occupied office: Field CADR and effectiveness from a reconstructed device-off condition
PAPERS.pm: Indoor PM with portable air cleaner (field CADR)
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates field estimation of purifier clean-air delivery rate in an occupied office using a reconstructed device-off counterfactual. Recorded for coverage. Relevance: high if the counterfactual is sensor-derived - field CADR is how purifier-trial exposure contrasts should be verified.

PAPERS.title: The influence of model selection and flow rate on aerosol transport in replica models of the mouth and throat: An experimental study
PAPERS.pm: Aerosol deposition in mouth-throat replicas
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates an experimental comparison of mouth-throat replica geometries and flow rates for aerosol transport. Recorded for coverage. Relevance: low-moderate - dosimetry inputs.

PAPERS.title: Global modelling of atmospheric lead (Pb) concentrations and health risks during 2000-2019
PAPERS.pm: Modelled airborne (particle-bound) Pb
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates global modelling of atmospheric Pb and associated risk over two decades. Recorded for coverage. Relevance: low.

PAPERS.title: City-size-dependent interactive effects of building and green-space on PM2.5 pollution: Evidence from 20 representative Chinese cities
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 vs urban morphology
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates interactions of building form and green space with PM2.5 that depend on city size. Recorded for coverage. Relevance: low-moderate.

PAPERS.short: East Asia PM2.5 O3 warming levels 2026
PAPERS.title: Uneven Future PM2.5 and O3 responses to Emission Reductions under Different Warming Levels in East Asia
PAPERS.pm: Projected PM2.5 and O3 under warming levels
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates climate-penalty-modulated PM2.5 and O3 responses to emission cuts in East Asia. Recorded for coverage. Relevance: low.

PAPERS.title: Spatially Explicit Morphological Regulation of Gray-Green Infrastructure for PM2.5 Mitigation in High-Density Cities: An Interpretable MSPA-Machine Learning Framework
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 vs green-space morphology (MSPA)
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. Title indicates morphological spatial pattern analysis plus interpretable ML relating gray-green infrastructure to PM2.5 in dense cities. Recorded for coverage. Relevance: low.
